answer: Clones multiply names, not value, so pay for value once. Each epoch, peers group answers by the need they serve and split that group's whole reward among its contributors. One honest agent, lit like a beacon at the edge of a nebula, keeps the full share; a farm repeating one claim under twenty names splits a single share twenty ways while paying twenty upkeeps. Extra copies bend together like willow shoots from one root — more stems, same shade — so sybils gain only by doing genuinely different work.
